gaps.note: telco.com publishes data sheets only; hardware documentation is on a support portal behind a login, whose contact is on telco.com/support.
gaps.wanted: the XM-7380 hardware installation guide, from the BATM support portal.

gaps.note: Sixteen of the 48 UNI ports are SFP+ and 32 are SFP (a count that rests on the borrowed NNI speed), and nothing held says which; all 48 are exported at 1g, the rate every one carries (see provenance.port-speeds).
The data sheet does not say the four right-hand ports are the 10G ones; 10g is BORROWED from the XM-7280 (see provenance.nni-speed).
Each UNI column is legended with one pair of numbers ("2/1" ... "48/47") and nothing held says which cage is which; the upper cage is drawn as the first number.
The two hot-swappable supplies are not on the front, so they (and presumably the fans) are at the rear, which nothing held shows.
No rate is stated for the SNMP out-of-band port; 1g is carried as a BORROWED value (see provenance.snmp-speed), not as a finding.

chassis.note: 1RU, 440 x 44 x 360 - the data sheet's "44 cm x 36 cm x 4.4 cm", "1U, 19-inch rack-mountable", 6.77 kg. The rack ears are not part of the face.

front-layout.note: POSITIONS ARE THE RENDER'S. Rectifying the four face corners (111.5,403 1540.5,401.5 1540.5,541.5 111.5,543 - square-on to within 2 px) onto the data sheet's 440 x 44, every cage, jack, lamp, vent and legend is placed from dark-run, glyph-cluster and centroid scans of that 10 px/mm image. The stencil master is used for arrangement and legends only. THE UPRIGHT LEGENDS (X-METRO 7380, CONSOLE, SNMP, the laser label's text) are rotate -90, which the renderer draws reading upward with the caps to the LEFT of the baseline - checked by rasterising: CONSOLE's glyphs land at x 372.1-373.3, clear of the USB jack at 375.5. L21 reports two of them as painted over, falsely and for two separate reasons in lint: its text-extent helper has the two right-angle cases swapped (a 270-degree mark's caps put to the right), which is the X-METRO 7380 line; and L21's placement boxes turn only a rotate-180 part, so the rotate-90 USB console is boxed as if lying flat (12 x 4.5 across x 371.8-383.8) and swallows CONSOLE whichever side its caps are on. Both L21 lines are in the baseline as false positives, pending a fix to lint.

lamps.note: Six status lamps in two columns (416.3 and 422.1 across, 7.0, 12.15 and 17.3 down), legended PWR1 / FAN1 / SNMP to the left and PWR2 / FAN2 / SYS to the right with bracket leaders, read top to bottom. No document says what any state means.

model.note: XM-7380 data sheet (telco.com 2026-08), "Compact High-Density Carrier Ethernet"; the faceplate prints X-METRO 7380.

nni-speed.note: BORROWED, NOT STATED. The XM-7380 data sheet does not say which of its ports the four at the right are; 10g is taken from the sibling XM-7280's data sheet, which calls its right-hand four "4x10G SFP NNI" on the same face layout; the nni-speed gap stays open.

port-speeds.note: "20 x 10G/1G SFP+, 32 x 1G/100M SFP" - 52 ports, and the face has 48 in the blocks and four at the right. WHICH OF THE 48 ARE SFP+ IS NOT DOCUMENTED - there is no port table and the three blocks are identical in the render - so all 48 are one group at 1g, the only rate every UNI cage is documented to carry ("10G/1G" SFP+ and "1G/100M" SFP), and the split is stated only in attrs.features.uni-mix. The count of SFP+ among them (16) itself rests on the NNI four being 10G, which is borrowed (see nni-speed).

ports.note: The 48 UNI ports are three stacked 2 x 8 blocks, std/sfp-ganged@1, upper row bail up and lower turned 180, on the measured 14.37, 14.64 and 14.39 pitches (columns 17.5-118.1, 138.1-240.55 and 260.7-361.45; rows 15.3 and 31.4), with the family's arrow strip between the rows. Each column is legended with one pair, 2/1 to 48/47; the upper cage is drawn as the first number (see the port-order gap). THE NUMERALS ARE PLACED WHERE PRINTED, measured by clustering their glyphs, up to about a millimetre either side of their columns, so L61 stays in the baseline for them on purpose. The four NNI ports at the right are a 1 x 4 row printed 1-4, each with two bar lamps above it - LNK/ACT to its left and SPEED to its right, as the two legends read. The render's NNI cages sit on a 13.93 pitch, which the 14.25-wide std/sfp-ganged@1 cannot, so they are drawn at 14.25 on the row's measured centre (402.2); the numerals and lamps are placed where printed, so L61 stays for them too.

power.note: "2 hot-swappable AC/DC power supplies provide 1+1 redundancy", "AC:220V, 100~240VAC | DC: -48V, -36~-72V". The front carries no supply, so the supplies (and presumably the fans) are at the rear, which nothing held shows; no consumption figure is published.

snmp-jack.note: THE SNMP JACK IS BARE - a metal-shielded RJ45 with no lamp windows, as on the XM-8102 - so it is std/rj45@2, and L76 stays in the baseline for it on purpose.

snmp-speed.note: BORROWED, NOT STATED. The ordering table lists "CONSOLE and SNMP ports for management" and gives no rate; 1g is taken from the TM-8104's OOB port on the maintainer's ruling for unstated management rates; the snmp-speed gap stays open.

sources.note: The data sheet (2026-08), the vendor render telco.com 2025/01/XM-7380new@2x.png (1678 px, square-on, about 3.25 px/mm on the face), and the NetZoom stencil "BATM X-Series" (2025-03-07), master X-Metro 7380 (CF). No installation guide is public.
